refutedOnReview: REFUTED as a dialect. The sources are real and I verified them, and they refute the framing rather than support it.  What I checked, live, on 2026-07-31:  1. https://www.victronenergy.com/media/pg/Cerbo_GX/en/installation.html — §3.5 exists and is titled "GX Touch 50 series & GX Touch 70 series". It states verbatim: "The GX Touch is connected using a single combined cable with: An HDMI connector (for video) A USB con
gotchas: There is nothing to drive here. It renders the GX's own Remote Console over HDMI. Any data a driver wants is on the GX, over victron-gx-modbus-tcp or victron-gx-mqtt.

Cable length is fixed at 2 m and the Cerbo GX manual carries a dedicated FAQ, Q22, 'Can I extend the cable between the Cerbo GX and the GX Touch 50 or 70?' — treat extension as a documented constraint, not an assumption.

USB port choice is model-dependent. Cerbo GX manual: on the first-generation Cerbo GX (BPP900450100) 'connect the USB connector to the USB port located right next to the HDMI port'; on the Cerbo GX MK2 (BPP900450110 / BPP900451100) 'you can connect the GX Touch to any of the three USB ports.'

Part numbers BPP900455050 / BPP900455150 / BPP900455070 / BPP900455170 are RETAIL-SOURCED. The Cerbo GX manual's technical-specifications tables give GX Touch resolutions, dimensions, IP ratings and cable length but print no part numbers for them. The one GX Touch part number that did surface on a Victron page is BPP90

There is also a protection cover (included from serial HQ2242 onwards) which 'does not fit the GX Touch 50 Flush and GX Touch 70 Flush versions' — irrelevant to a driver, recorded so the Flush/non-Flush split is not mistaken for a functional one.
